entities.summary:
Charles d'Angennes de Rambouillet was a French Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal who played a crucial role in the Catholic Church's governance during the tumultuous 16th century. He was appointed as the Archbishop of Reims in 1561, a position that gave him significant influence over the Church's politics and liturgy.

Born in 1528, Rambouillet was educated at the University of Paris and later studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University in Rome. He was ordained as a priest in 1552 and quickly rose through the ranks of the Church, becoming the Bishop of Meaux in 1558 and the Archbishop of Reims in 1561.

During his tenure, Rambouillet worked tirelessly to promote the interests of the French monarchy and the Catholic Church. He was a strong supporter of the Habsburgs and played a key role in the Catholic Church's efforts to counter the Protestant Reformation.

Rambouillet's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime. He played a significant role in shaping the Catholic Church's response to the Protestant Reformation, and his policies and decisions continue to influence the Church's governance to this day.

In conclusion, Charles d'Angennes de Rambouillet was a pivotal figure in the Catholic Church's history, whose contributions to the Church's governance and politics continue to be felt today.

The death of Charles d'Angennes de Rambouillet on March 23, 1587, marked the end of an era in the Catholic Church. His passing was mourned by Catholics across Europe, and he was remembered as a devoted servant of the Church.

In the centuries that followed, Rambouillet's legacy continued to shape the Catholic Church's response to the Protestant Reformation. His policies and decisions continue to influence the Church's governance and politics, and he remains an important figure in the Church's history.
